add.title: Transgender rights in Canada (Wikipedia; Prisons section)
add.summary: Wikipedia 'Transgender rights in Canada', Prisons section (accessed 4 Oct 2026): at the federal level the Correctional Service of Canada (CSC) permits gender-diverse offenders to request placement or transfer to a men's or women's institution aligned with their gender identity or expression, regardless of anatomy or the sex marker on their identification documents; requests are assessed individually and may be refused where an unresolved 'overriding health or safety concern' exists under CSC's 2022 gender-diversity policy. The article reports that as of 2025 CSC recorded 90 self-identified transgender women in federal custody - 73 housed in men's institutions and 17 in women's - and that between fiscal years 2017-18 and 2024-25 CSC received 129 placement/transfer requests from people assigned male at birth to women's institutions (35 approved, 72 denied, 22 withdrawn). Provincial correctional policies vary and the article does not document a New Brunswick provincial-jail placement rule; the federal policy is the framework a trans prisoner in federal custody in New Brunswick stands under. The Correctional Investigator has criticised the policy's unclear 'health or safety' override criteria and the lack of a dedicated abuse-reporting mechanism.
